_comment: DS-A003 decrease-only parity debt, bucketed by typed owner or CSS-variable namespace. --update-baseline may only tighten existing buckets; a new nonzero bucket requires reviewed manual adoption.

_adoptions.r1p-closure-2026-07-27: Reviewed manual adoption (R1-P closure): (a) declared-but-unemitted.BrandPalette 0->30 and total 23->53 — W-B's optional 1:1 palette capability fields (delta contract: unauthored fields emit nothing by design); (b) emitted-but-unconsumed sidebar 5->10, total 241->245 — channels previously declared-and-unconsumed inside the rottay/bithire extensions, now compiler-emitted and census-visible (transfer, not new dead surface); consumption or retirement is the Kimi wire-or-retire lane. input 2->1 tightened. Codex ratification required.
_adoptions.lane-a-tint-enumerability-2026-08-10: Reviewed manual adoption, same class as (b) above. emitted-but-unconsumed.tint 0->10, total unchanged at 245 (actual 205). The tint ramp was ALREADY emitted into all three vertical artifacts; setTintScaleVariables built its keys with a ternary behind an indirection, which the parity graph's keyCandidates cannot resolve, so the emitter was census-invisible. Spelling the five scale prefixes as literals changed the CENSUS, not the runtime. Evidence, stated precisely after audit: the rewrite is output-identical by VALUE — same name templates, same value template, same guards, same insertion order — and the tenant-theme digest actuals are identical between HEAD and the working tree. Artifact byte-identity is NOT evidence here and must not be cited as such: build-vertical-artifacts reads dist, dist is stale and still carries the previous ternary emitter writing oklch, so the artifacts were never produced by the emitter this change rewrites. Two of the three pinned tenant-theme digests do not reproduce at all; that failure is byte-identical at HEAD and is pre-existing, not caused by this change. Transfer, not new dead surface. Total ratcheted 245 -> 205, the measured actual. NOT a retirement candidate as filed: --ds-tint-4 is read by brand-themes/fixtures/themanagementmiami, and DS-internal read counts exclude the three apps. Retirement of any tint step is a design ruling on a closed normative scale and belongs to its own lane.
